graph.title: Button Mouse Control (Arduino Leonardo, five pushbuttons)
notes: The part list is the same as step 1. Only the button labels changed, because the image wires the leftmost button to pin 6 and the rightmost to pin 2. The schematic agrees. The step 1 labels had this order reversed.
Button-to-pin mapping from the image: btn1=pin 6 (mouse click), btn2=pin 5 (right), btn3=pin 4 (left), btn4=pin 3 (down), btn5=pin 2 (up). The mapping of pins 2-5 to directions comes from the sketch.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the rows f-j half is at the top, so those holes are written 'b'. The rows a-e half, with the signal wires and resistors, is written 't'.

Rail names follow the same geometry. The rails beside rows f-j (the top rail in the image) are 'bp'/'bn', and the 5V line is 'bp'. The rails beside rows a-e (the bottom rail in the image) are 'tp'/'tn', and ground is 'tn'.
Each button straddles the centre gap. Side 1 is the upper pair of legs in rows f, wired to 5V. Side 2 is the lower pair in row e, wired to the signal wire and the 10k pulldown resistor.

Button columns are 6/8, 11/13, 16/18, 21/23 and 26/28. Each resistor sits in the lower-left leg column of its button, row a, and runs to the ground rail. The signal wires land in that same column at row b, or row c for pin 6.
Rail hole numbers are estimated from the image. Only the rail strip itself matters electrically.
The black wire goes to the first GND pin beside 5V, written GND.1.
The micro-USB cable to the computer is not in the hardware list, so it is not included.
